answer.explanation: The application service computes business logic over the fridge's stock state. It takes the minimum of requested units and on-hand stock, works out the shortfall, and decides when an urgent red-cell request may be covered with O-negative stock. It then hands the results to the fridge (take) and to Fulfilment. The stock allocation and substitution rules sit in the service, not in the fridge aggregate or a domain policy. The fridge only exposes onHand and take, so the calculation is done outside the entity and the result is passed back to it.
